notes:
The walkthrough has no [n] bullets at all -- it is three prose paragraphs with a wikitable between them -- so source_bullets numbers those three blocks: [1] the 'speak to Anastase' paragraph, [2] the 'you must discover eleven Geomagnetic Founts' paragraph together with the table it introduces, [3] the closing 'return to Anastase' sentence. Every one of the eleven founts is fully specified in that table with a zone and a grid ref, so all eleven get their own properly zoned step rather than one nil-zone Geomagnetic Fount that would match everywhere; they share a group because the page gives no order and the hints are handed out all at once.

Nothing in this quest is observable. The Prototype attuner is carried in from 'Researchers from the West' -- the page assumes you already hold it and never says it is granted here -- so it is not evidence (rule 3), and it is deliberately NOT listed in items either: you hold it for the whole quest, so putting it on all eleven fount steps would light every fount as ready-to-act from the first second and distinguish nothing. The founts award only experience points, so there is no key item to hang a rung on and the ladder relies on the session latch throughout.

The second paragraph's 'asking Anastase about his predictions' is not a second visit worth a rung -- it is the same NPC as step 1 and the table already gives every location -- so it is folded into step 1's note. The two '(Optional)' asides in the table belong to OTHER quests entirely (a Stone Monument for An Explorer's Footsteps in North Gustaberg, a Cermet Headstone holding the Water fragment for Zilart Mission 5 in La Theine Plateau) and are not steps here; they are kept in the relevant fount's note because they are on the way. The Unity-warp and survival-guide lines are travel advice, not steps.

steps.note: you must have zoned out of and back into Ru'Lude Gardens after the previous quest; pick the FIRST option to expand the warp list. Asking him about his predictions is the same conversation and yields the eleven hints, so it is not a separate rung.

'Green Light' -- a green light at the end of a dark prison. Reached only through Bostaunieux Oubliette; the content-level-122 Unity warp lands beside the zone entrance, and you should not drop down after zoning out. 900 EXP.

'Clear Waters' -- reached through Dangruf Wadi, on the north side of the river near the entrance, up on a rock. 750 EXP. An Explorer's Footsteps has a Stone Monument further east in the cave at the end of the path.
'Crowned Tower' -- at the entrance of the Outer Horutoto Ruins, on the platform above the staircase leading down. 320 EXP; the survival guide halves the walk from Windurst.

'Deep Cliffs' -- inside the valley, just outside the Ordelle's Caves exit near Morbolger; you have to run the caves to get there. 600 EXP. Zilart Mission 5's Cermet Headstone with the Water fragment is further southwest at the end of the chasm.
'Windmill' -- walk across the spine to reach it. 500 EXP; the Gusgen Mines survival guide is the quick way in.
'Dust Cloud' -- between a rock formation and the east wall. 500 EXP; the Buburimu Peninsula survival guide gets you close.
'Lakeside' -- reached only through King Ranperre's Tomb. 750 EXP.
'Swamps' -- southeast corner, next to the Luremarsh, standing in a puddle. 500 EXP.
'Backbone' -- northeast corner of the square. 500 EXP.
'Crags' -- at the top of Parradamo Tor. 900 EXP.

'Silver' -- top of the mountain, on the trail behind the Ice Waterfall, which the page says DISAPPEARS when no weather is present (so it is there only while weather is up); directly beside Home Point Crystal #1. 2000 EXP, the largest of the eleven.
only after all eleven founts are attuned; nothing observable reports how many you have done.

notes:
A two-rung quest and the page is unambiguous about it. Bullet 3 is not a step: it is the OUTCOME of the trade -- the fishing report Katsunaga reads back to you -- and its five sub-bullets are the contents of that report, not things you do. Both real steps are on Katsunaga at Mhaura (H-9), so they are one marker and readiness looks ahead across them; the tuna is what actually matters.

Neither 'After the walkthrough' section is steps. 'Fish List' is an eleven-page reference table of every catchable fish in the game -- it is what the report tells you, rendered out -- and 'Notes' is a pointer at the discussion tab for skilling up. The reward is statistics and a Vorseal unlock, so there is nothing to hold and no step carries evidence; the trade is unobservable and the ladder falls back on the session latch.

'Quest Reqs: Level 20 Fishing skill' is a CRAFT/skill gate, not a character level and not a job, so gates.level stays null and jobs stays empty -- putting 20 in level would gate this at character level 20, which is wrong in both directions. There is no observable predicate for fishing skill either, hence the flag. Fame reads 'Other', which is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing, so region is null while FLevel 2 is kept.

ADVERSARY (stage D): confidence lowered high -> medium. The ladder itself survives every attack -- two rungs, both on Katsunaga at Mhaura (H-9), source order preserved, bullet 3 correctly rejected as the outcome of the trade, no evidence anywhere and therefore no double-use and no empty all-list. But the quest carries an unmodellable gate: 'Quest Reqs: Level 20 Fishing skill' is already flagged skill_gate_unmodelled, and the rubric puts 'the ladder is right but a gate is unmodellable' at medium, not high. Nothing was removed.

THE FISHING GATE IS NOW MODELLED. The header reads `|Quest Reqs=Level 20 [[Fishing]] skill`, so it is an ENTRY condition and not a mid-quest cost, and it resolves to res/skills.lua 48 with a level threshold of 20. The gate is recorded as a LEVEL, and it is deliberately one the runtime may never grey a marker on. Packet 0x062 reports NATURAL skill -- the number the in-game menu shows -- and equipment adds on top of it invisibly: Trainee's Spectacles give +1 Fishing and the menu still reads 1 when the effective skill is 2. Since the NPC checks the effective number, natural-below-threshold means "cannot tell", not "cannot start", so core/prereq.lua returns nil there and the marker goes BLACK rather than grey. Above the threshold is still a definite true, so the false yellow is removed without a false grey replacing it. A craft RANK is different and does grey, because no equipment moves the stored result of a rank-up test.

steps.note: one tuna; repeatable, so this is the whole quest every time round

notes:
Three good evidence points -- Broken flying machine, Levitation device, Whirring engine -- all key items that resolve, all granted at the step that earns them and none repeated, so this ladder actually tracks.

Start: the header names Jeridade in Upper Jeuno and bullet 1 says to approach the chocobo stable at (G-7). Those agree rather than conflict -- Jeridade is the giver standing there and the cutscene fires on approach -- so the marker goes on Jeridade and no start_disagrees flag is warranted. 'the chocobo stable' is a descriptive phrase, not an entity the page names, so it stays in the note.

Bullet 6 spans two zones in one sentence -- get Doctor Status from ANY Strange Apparatus, which the page says explicitly cannot be the Fei'Yin one, then come back to Fei'Yin and examine that one -- so it is split into steps 6 and 7. Step 6 deliberately carries no zone: 'any' is the instruction, and Strange Apparatus is not in the ambiguous-NPC set, so a zone-less marker on the nearest one is exactly right. Doctor Status is a status, not a key item, so neither half is observable.

Bullet 5 says only 'open a coffer in Ve'Lugannon Palace'. It never writes 'Treasure Coffer', and coffers move, so the target is none rather than a guessed name -- the zone and the Levitation device still carry the rung. The Ve'Lugannon Coffer Key resolves and is recorded; how you get it (5,000 gil from a Curio Vendor Moogle) is not an alternative way to do the step, so items_partial stays false there.

The cluster requirement is the real loss. The apparatus wants 38 elemental crystal clusters, 'any combination of elements works' -- eight different item ids in any mix, which is neither one resolvable name (Elemental Crystal Cluster resolves to nothing; Fire Cluster and friends are never named on the page) nor an alternation this schema can hold. Step 9 therefore carries no items and sets items_partial, with the count in the note.

Bullet 2's The Celestial Nexus II gets no zone: the page never says where it is entered, only that any difficulty will do. The Quest Reqs line adds 'Must have completed Awakening' -- a mission, not a quest -- so it is NOT put into gates.prev, where a title that can never match a quest would gate this quest shut forever; it is flagged instead. Previous stays as the header gives it.

Not steps: the Boisterous Jackal sub-bullet is marked 'Optional', is about saving time on the Omega whistle rather than this quest, and is then contradicted by the page's own July 2026 update saying it is unnecessary -- so it is recorded here and nowhere else. The '== Maps ==' tables are thumbnail galleries, the party-coffer advice is tactics, and the note that a Levitus inventory item exists but you get the key item instead is trivia. The Levitus key is the header's Reward and does not resolve as a key item anyway, so it is not evidence (rule 7).

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 9: hence items_partial with nothing in items.

steps.note: the cutscene fires on APPROACHING the chocobo stable at (G-7); there may be nothing to click. You may have to zone after finishing Full Speed Ahead!. The header's giver Jeridade is the entity standing there, so the marker is put on him rather than on an unnamed stable.

the battlefield The Celestial Nexus II, on any difficulty. The page never says which zone it is entered from and names no mob, so both are left empty rather than guessed; it also requires the mission Awakening to be accessible.
the page gives no grid for Mapitoto; the chocobo stable of bullet 1 is (G-7) and he is the quest's handler there.

map 1. Every apparatus is behind a fake wall: come in at the basement (H-9, map 1) or warp Fauregandi > Fei'Yin > Home Point #2, then back upstairs from (E-7, map 2) to (G/H-6, map 1) and run through the wall.

the page says only 'a coffer', so no target name is invented; coffers move anyway. The key is 5,000 gil from a Curio Vendor Moogle. In a PARTY (not alliance) everyone in the zone who still needs it gets the key item -- but only if the opener is someone who needs it.

Doctor Status, from ANY Strange Apparatus except the Fei'Yin one -- the page is explicit that Fei'Yin cannot grant it, and that once obtained it survives the trip back. No zone is recorded because 'any' is the instruction. Do NOT trade this quest's items to an apparatus outside Fei'Yin: they are lost. Doctor Status is a status, not a key item, so this step is unobservable.
second half of bullet 6: back to the Fei'Yin apparatus, with Doctor Status, and examine it.
both together, and only to the Fei'Yin apparatus

38 elemental crystal clusters, any combination of elements, traded as stacks. The page names no individual cluster and 'Elemental Crystal Cluster' is not an item, so the requirement cannot be written down at all.

notes:
Five investigations, each with its own internal chain, and bullet 2 says outright that 'the recordings can be completed in any order' -- so the five share a group and all draw at once. What they do NOT get is a rung each for every NPC inside them. A case runs contact NPC > witness NPC after a game-time hour > aim the photopticator at a scripted scene > report to Balakaf > back to the contact, and not one link of that is observable: no key item, no drop, nothing a packet reports. Expanding all five into twenty-odd untrackable rungs would be exactly the noise the pilot warned about, so each case is one step on the NPC you actually have to walk to first, with the whole chain in its note. Bullet 2 is cited on all five because its mechanics -- one case per Vana'diel day, talk to Balakaf between cases, zone before retrying a failed recording -- govern every one of them.

Bullet 2 is itself not a step; it is the rules of the minigame. The only observable thing in the quest is the Photopticator key item from bullet 1, which is step 1's evidence and the last rung anything can confirm; everything after it rides the session latch.

Every case is time-gated on Vana'diel clock time -- 15:00, 5:00, 14:00, 12:00 and 20:00 -- and capped at one per game day. Game time is invisible to the addon, so a marker will happily point you at an NPC hours too early. That, plus the ambiguity below, is why this is medium rather than high.

The 'Completion' section is read as steps and its bullets restart at [1], noted on each. Its bullet 2, returning to Balakaf for the Imperial Pieces, is the real end of the quest and is also what bullet 7's last sub-bullet ('Speak with Balakaf after completing all records') means. Its bullet 1 -- go round all five contacts again to hear the results -- is harder: it may genuinely be a final round, or it may just be the Completion section restating the per-case 'After talking to Balakaf, talk to <contact>' lines that are already folded into each case step. It is recorded as an optional group so that it draws without ever holding the ladder up, and the doubt is recorded here.

Fame reads 'none', which is not one of the nine regions, so region is null; the raw string is kept. Repeatable is 'no'. The reward list is a reward, not a step.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 3: Ulamaal (K-12), then Qutiba for the clue, then Ratihb (J-12) after 5:00 and pick the option matching Qutiba's clue, then Zubyahn (K-12); record shortly after pumpkin head reaches the front of the queue and you succeed by catching him leaving the counter and rejoining the back of the line.
  step 6: Ahaadah (G-6), then Mathlouq (F-5), then Nijaom (F-7) after 20:00; record once the second person appears and you succeed by catching the medicine changing hands and the pair parting.
  step 12: This is also what bullet 7's closing sub-bullet, 'Speak with Balakaf after completing all records', refers to.

'A Pickpocket's Paradise', from 15:00. Zyfhil (F-8) first, then Talwahn (F-8) after 15:00; start recording once the thief (Hume Male, Face 8, Hair B) is standing behind the visitor and you succeed by catching him pickpocketing. Then Balakaf, then Zyfhil again. One case per Vana'diel day; zone before retrying a failure.
'Special of the Day', from 5:00. Then Balakaf, then Ulamaal again. The page gives no grid for Qutiba.

'Smells Like a Rat', from 14:00. The page names two contacts standing together at (F-10), Mushayra and Hadahda; one marker covers both. Then Tehf Kimasnahya (F-8) after 14:00; the housewife enters, stops, then moves toward the pillar -- start recording as she moves -- and you succeed by catching the Qiqirn dodging round the pillar. Then Balakaf, then Mushayra and Hadahda again.

'An Early Exit', from 12:00. The shortest case -- Hishahma (K-8) after 12:00 is the only contact. Four soldiers run past left to right and back; begin recording on their THIRD pass as the lead soldier reaches the right of the screen, and you succeed by capturing all four on that pass and the rear soldier missing on the fourth. Then Balakaf, then Hishahma again.
'Strangers in the Night', from 20:00. Then Balakaf, then Ahaadah again.
